subject: Private deployment telemetry exemptions, customer key split & transfer carve-outs
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novamed.health>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-08T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment questions — telemetry & key custody

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we finalize procurement for the private VPC deployment, a few specific privacy/ops items came up from our legal and security teams that we need to capture in the DPA and the accompanying SOW:

1) Telemetry carve-outs: we require that application-level prompts and model outputs that contain PHI (sample streams from pilot) are excluded from any telemetry retention or analytics. We understand operational logs (scheduler, infra alerts) are necessary for support, but we need a clear separation and retention limits for telemetry derived from customer traffic.

2) Customer-controlled keys: NovaMed must retain CMK control with no plaintext transfer to Redwood. We may accept escrow under narrow circumstances (court order) but need explicit process and notification windows.

3) Data transfer carve-outs: certain pilot datasets cannot leave US-based infrastructure. Any fallbacks or operator interventions that might route to other regions must be explicitly disallowed or require documented exceptions.

Can you send a proposed mapping (who does what) and suggested DPA wording? Attaching our annotated DPA and a short requirements list.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of InfoSec, NovaMed
Attachment: NovaMed_DPA_questions_v2.pdf (pdf, 245KB)

From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novamed.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-08T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — telemetry & key custody

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on the objectives and I've looped in Marissa (security & compliance) and Karthik (private deployment/product). We'll put together a concise responsibilities matrix and a short DPA redline focused on three buckets: telemetry scope & retention; key custody/escrow procedure; regional routing/fallback guardrails.

Two quick clarifications before we draft:
- For telemetry, do you want absolute exclusion (no collection) for any traffic labeled PHI, or is pseudonymized telemetry acceptable for service reliability?
- For escrow, is a notarized, sealed escrow (controlled by a named trustee) acceptable, or do you require alternative legal tooling?

We will send a proposed matrix by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: —

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-09T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Private deployment questions — telemetry & key custody (internal notes)

Jordan / Karthik — drafting notes below to feed back to NovaMed. High level proposal:

1) Telemetry slicing and retention
- "User-facing PHI traffic": no telemetry collection by default. Redwood will support a per-route flag (config in the tenant manifest) to disable telemetry capture.
- "Pseudonymized operational metrics": we can emit aggregated token-level metrics (latency, error rate) with deterministic hashing, retention 30 days by default; longer retention only with explicit customer opt-in.
- "Support snapshots": ephemeral traces for debugging (up to 72 hours), available only via on-demand customer request and must be explicitly authorized in the SOW.

2) Customer keys and escrow
- Customer retains CMK in their KMS (customer-managed keys). Redwood never stores plaintext keys.
- Escrow protocol: trustee-held escrow only upon court order; require 30-day notice to customer + signed attestation steps. Include key-rotation notification windows.

3) Data transfer / operator interventions
- Default routing: US regions only for NovaMed.
- Emergency fallback: operator-assisted migration to alternative region is disallowed unless pre-authorized through a documented exception including signed approval from NovaMed security.

I've attached a short matrix and a redline DPA excerpt. Please add technical notes (Karthik) around feasibility and any infra constraints.

Attachments: privdep-telemetry-exemptions-matrix.xlsx, DPA_draft_for_novamed.pdf

-M

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-09T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private deployment questions — telemetry & key custody (internal notes)

Thanks Marissa — technical clarifications / suggestions to include in the SOW/DPA redline:
- Implementation for route-level telemetry toggles exists in the control plane; we'll need a tenant manifest change and a migration window (2 weeks) for the pilot to flip flags safely. Note that disabling telemetry removes KV-cache diagnostic signals — we recommend a debug-mode toggle that streams stripped traces to a customer-owned S3 for troubleshooting (no Redwood retention).
- KMS: customer CMK integration supported via KMS proxy; we never decrypt on a Redwood-managed node. For escrow we can support trustee escrow but need to define key-release protocol and HSM signing ops; suggest a short appendix describing the trustee workflow and audit trail.
- Operator break-glass: must be logged to an immutable audit trail in customer-controlled drives (we can push logs to a customer bucket). Also add explicit SLA for required notification within 24 hours of any manual intervention.

I'll inline these into the DPA redline and the matrix.

-Karthik

From: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novamed.health>, Julian Park <julian.park@novamed.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-10T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed responsibilities matrix + DPA redline (attached)

Hi Elena / Julian — attached is our proposed responsibilities matrix and a short DPA redline that implements the points above:

- Telemetry: route-level "no-collect" flag; pseudonymized aggregated metrics only; 30-day default retention; support snapshots gated by customer authorization and stored in customer-owned S3 for 72 hours.
- Keys: customer-managed CMK, Redwood will use KMS proxy; escrow only via named trustee on court order with 30-day notice.
- Regional routing: tenant pinned to US regions; operator fallback requires documented, signed exception.
- Operator interventions: mandatory push of all intervention logs to customer bucket; 24-hour notification SLA; immutable audit trail.

Attachments: privdep-telemetry-exemptions-matrix.xlsx, DPA_draft_for_novamed.pdf

Please review; if this aligns with your legal/security view we can prep a final DPA and execute the SOW. If you want any language tightened (e.g., specific notice windows, escrow trustee identity), tell us and we'll update the draft.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: privdep-telemetry-exemptions-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), DPA_draft_for_novamed.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novamed.health>

Jordan — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few editorial asks before legal signs:
- Add explicit language that telemetry exclusion applies to backups and any long-term archives.
- Escrow: name of accepted trustee(s) to be included in the SOW appendix, and the 30-day notice should require proof of legal compulsion.
- Operator notification SLA: change to 12 hours for critical interventions affecting PHI processing.

If you can patch those three items and return a redline, we can move to finalize the DPA and route procurement. Please include the Confluence link for the operational runbook once available.

Thanks — will aim to sign after the small edits.

Elena

- Escrow: we will insert trustee name options (recommended trustee list) and require documented proof of legal compulsion for any release; timeframe remains 30 days from notification.
- Intervention SLA: updated to 12 hours for critical PHI-impacting interventions.

I'll attach the updated redline and Confluence runbook link once ready. Next steps: final DPA -> signatures (DocuSign) -> procurement/PO.

Jordan
